intro: Keep long streams comfortable and intentional. Set the planned stream length and automatic mode chooses the break cadence, shows a five-minute warning, takes a five-minute break by default, restores the last live scene, and moves to the selected ending scene at the limit without stopping the broadcast.

labels.previous: Restore the scene I was using

sections.title: 1. Turn on the guard
sections.description: Choose the app that owns your program scene. The extension remains inactive until a genuine live signal arrives.
sections.notice: This extension changes scenes only. It never starts or stops streaming, and test events cannot cause a real scene change.

sections.title: 2. Plan the stream length
sections.description: Choose the maximum live-session length and the detected scene shown when that limit is reached.
sections.notice: The ending scene is a reminder and handoff point; the extension deliberately leaves the broadcast running for your raid or manual ending flow.

sections.title: 3. Schedule breaks
sections.description: Automatic mode calculates the cadence from the planned stream length: 60 minutes produces a break at 30 minutes, while streams of two hours or more use an hourly cadence. Breaks last five minutes by default.
sections.notice: A break is skipped when it would overlap the five-minute end warning. The stream limit always wins.

sections.title: 4. Five-minute reminder overlay
sections.description: Show a clear countdown before a break or the stream limit, plus the remaining time while on break.

sections.title: 5. Connect the built-in scene helper
sections.description: Import the included Streamer.bot package and approve its one triggerless Scene Controller action.
sections.notice: Do not attach a trigger to Scene Controller. StreamBridge calls it with a one-use authorization token and exact validated provider, connection, and scene values.
